children: Crude oil traded near $95 per barrel on Thursday after rallying for five straight sessions, underpinned by escalating hostilities in the Middle East and Eastern Europe that heightened concerns over supply disruptions.
A container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday after being hit by unidentified projectiles, while Iran-backed Houthi forces continued missile and drone attacks across Saudi Arabia.
More oil tankers are steering clear of their usual crude-loading areas, indicating that increased Iranian attacks on shipping are disrupting export operations.

Meanwhile, Russia accused Ukraine of striking two oil refineries on Wednesday, including the 400,000-barrel-per-day Ryazan facility, violating an “energy ceasefire” announced by US President Donald Trump.
In the US, API data revealed that crude inventories fell by 11.1 million barrels last week, marking the largest decline since June 2025.

title: Oil Holds Advance on Heightened Supply Risks
